exercise.name: 90 degrees Heel Touch

reference.title: 90 degrees Heel Touch
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; page could not be read at authoring time, movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)

exercise.mechanics: Isolation (hip extension and flexion with the knees held at 90 degrees; anti-extension core)

breathing.pattern: Inhale as the heels lower, exhale as the legs come back to tabletop.

prescription.progression: Slower lowering, then straighten the knees a little (longer lever)

cues.text: Lie on your back, arms by your sides; hips and knees bent 90 degrees, shins level (tabletop).
Keep the knees at 90 degrees and lower both heels toward the mat; low back stays flat.
Lightly touch the heels to the mat; do not rest.
Breathe out and draw the thighs back to vertical.

mistakes.mistake: Low back arching as the heels lower
mistakes.fix: Shorten the range: tap only as low as the back stays flat.

mistakes.mistake: Knee angle opening to reach the floor
mistakes.fix: Keep the knees at 90 degrees; the movement comes from the hips.

mistakes.mistake: Dropping the heels onto the mat
mistakes.fix: Touch lightly and come straight back up.

kinematics.norm: About 90 degrees in tabletop (thighs vertical), lowering until the heels touch (clinical opinion)
Heels lightly touch the mat at the bottom (clinical opinion)
Pelvis stays on the mat; low back flat (clinical opinion; Drysdale 2004 for abdominal bracing)

sources.title: GymVisual #9306, 90 degrees Heel Touch, video (movement reference)
Drysdale, Earl and Hertel 2004, surface EMG of the abdominal muscles during pelvic-tilt and abdominal-hollowing exercises (J Athl Train 39(1):32-36)
Escamilla et al. 2006, electromyographic analysis of traditional and nontraditional abdominal exercises: implications for rehabilitation and training (Phys Ther 86(5):656-671; PubMed 16649890)
McGill 1998, low back exercises: evidence for improving exercise regimens (Phys Ther 78(7):754-765; PMID 9672547)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Pregnancy and postpartum (diastasis recti): get individual guidance before dynamic trunk-flexion or legs-off-the-floor work.
modify: Tap one heel at a time (dead bug legs).

muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis and transversus keep the pelvis tilted back as the legs lower and pull it level; the anti-extension demand rises as the heels go down (clinical opinion; Escamilla 2006 for lower abdominal exercises).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Control the lowering and lift the thighs back to vertical.
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Control the lowering and lift the thighs back to vertical.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Help hold the ribs and pelvis together.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Help hold the ribs and pelvis together.
